author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Chester’s Planning Board has continued a public hearing on the proposed Village at Buxton Farm until September 30, giving the town’s engineering consultant more time to complete an environmental review and evaluate the latest project plans.

The proposal calls for 34 detached one- and two-bedroom rental homes at 611 Haverhill Road under Chester’s fair-market housing ordinance. Developer David Haddad requested the delay because the consultant’s reports were not ready for the board’s September 9 meeting.

Testing found PFAS in soil at the former farm field, where biosolids had previously been spread, but did not detect the chemicals in groundwater. An Edgewater Environmental Services report said the finding does not automatically prevent development. It recommended keeping affected soil on the property, minimizing disturbance, stabilizing or capping exposed areas and using erosion controls.

The homes would share one well. The developer said groundwater monitoring would continue and that the project would follow any additional environmental requirements. The next hearing is expected to give the board and residents a fuller record on both the PFAS management plan and Chester’s review of the housing proposal.
dek: The Planning Board moved its review of a proposed 34-home rental community to September 30 while engineers finish environmental and plan reviews.
headline: Chester delays Buxton Farm housing hearing for PFAS review
